posts.cooked:
I saw this article on top 10 board games with positive female representation online yesterday, and I thought I'd share it here. 

Spoiler alert: Sentinels of the Multiverse makes the list. My wife says she probably would've ranked it higher because they're original characters with rich backstories. I'd probably agree, but it's great to see it on the list. We have often played with an "all-lady" team and we kick butt.

Great job, Greater Than Games!

http://www.boardgamequest.com/top-ten-games-with-positive-female-representations/

posts.name: dpt
posts.cooked: At a GenCon panel I went to on diversity in games, there was a big call-out to Sentinels for its diversity. Not just for the obvious thing like the number of women on the cast, but the wide variety of other features that are well fleshed-out. In particular, one of the panelists had Ex-Patriette as a personal hero, because she was missing an eye, the same that the panelist was blind in. (It also helped that both the panelist and Ex-Patriette were female.)

posts.name: Silverleaf
posts.cooked:
We also have non-human and non-gender-binary people, as well as a decent age range. I'd like a little more diversity in body types, but mostly it's pretty good.

And disabilities - Fixer is blind, Expat has one eye, AZ needs to be in his suit or cryo chamber which is seriously restricting, Visionary essentially has brain damage that might kill her, Parse has Asperger's (arguably not a disability but it does cause problems in everyday life).

I'm beyond bored of the fact that so many other games out there stick to the old "straight white male as default" pattern. Those of us who aren't straight white males should be represented too!
